about: Every known difference between the web and native renderers on the golden documents. key: web#i is the i-th web block, native#j the j-th native block, .field the differing field. side: which renderer departs from the format or the other renderer (web, native) or by-design. A difference not listed here fails scripts/golden-docs; an entry that stops matching also fails, so the list cannot rot.

differences.reason: web numbers an unpublished marker by its position in source_entities (renderInlineSourceRef: indexOf+1), native numbers by first citation in reading order (Builder.addCite); the published path (manifest anchors) also numbers by reading order, so the web unpublished path is the odd one

native drops a first heading equal to the page title because the native page draws the headline itself (TextureDoc.swift failure item 13); web draws it. The title is page chrome, so this is an agreed difference unless web also drops it

an empty paragraph is valid in the schema; web draws an empty

(a blank gap), native drops it (failure item 4). Native's behaviour is the better one; web should skip empty paragraphs
a whitespace-only paragraph: same as the empty paragraph
ordered_list attrs.start: web renders <ol> without a start attribute, so a list that starts at 3 counts from 1; native honours start
same: second item of the list that starts at 3
a list_item with two paragraphs: web concatenates their inline content with no separator ("item.Second"); native keeps two blocks, the second without a marker
the second paragraph of the list item exists only on native (see the previous entry)
web's Markdown renderer flattens a nested list item to depth 1; native keeps depth 2
a Markdown rule (---) after a fenced code block: web draws a paragraph holding "---", native a rule
